content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm trying to connect an analog amplifier with an asynchronous pulse generator, but can't figure out how to achieve this using [product_name] software. My goal is to use an analog input (amplifier 0/4-20mA) to adjust the preset running time for an asynchronous pulse generator that controls a motor output. Is this possible?

Hi, Which generation of [product_name] hardware and which software version are you using? Starting from hardware version [article_no] with software [version_no], the asynchronous pulse generator supports reference functionality. You simply open the pulse generator and reference TH and TL to the analog amplifier. For older [product_name] hardware, you can still achieve this by building a pulse generator using on-delay and off-delay blocks manually. In versions older than [article_no], the pulse generator lacks reference functionality, but on-/off-delay is available.

analysis.insight_summary: The main challenge is users are unable to connect an analog amplifier input to change the preset time of an asynchronous pulse generator within [product_name] software. There is confusion due to differences in hardware and software versions, which affects the ability to implement this function.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the analog amplifier input to directly influence the timing behavior of the pulse generator through the software, seeking an easy and direct way to integrate analog input with timing logic.
